problem: Find all triples $(a,b,c)$ of distinct positive integers so that there exists a subset $S$ of the positive integers for which for all positive integers $n$ exactly one element of the triple $(an,bn,cn)$ is in $S$.
answer: (a, b, c) \text{ such that the ratios of any two are not perfect cubes}
